text:
The most beautiful head was falling

toward the side of dreams; summer

was a jasmine without borders, and in her hand

the day floated like a blue handkerchief.


And her mouth suddenly was falling

toward the side of kisses; summer

held her in the palm of its hand,

made of love, oh, what melancholy!


Along the shores of this love a river crossed;

over this love there was a palm tree:

water of time and sky-poetry.


And the river carried away everything of mine;

the hand and the summer and my palm tree

of poetry. Oh, what melancholy!

translation.title: The Most Beautiful Head Was Falling...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Carranza's dreamward movement and the refrain of melancholy as the river carries everything away.
